<a id="s0-p1"></a>[0¶1] This document is the contract for what `pcrec --emit-ir` prints: its sections, their columns, and what is and is not promised about each. It conforms to `docs/spec/table_contract.md` and adds only what is specific to this listing. `docs/spec/cli.md` §2 is the flag's own reference entry. The listing's history is `docs/dev/history/ir_listing_record.md`, which is not normative.

<a id="s1"></a>
## 1. What the listing is

- <a id="s1-p1"></a>[1¶1] It is a DEBUG listing. It is complete for CONTROL STRUCTURE (every label, every instruction, every branch target, every choice point and its preference order) and LOSSY ON OPERANDS: a class scan shows its rung role, not its class membership; MRL clamp arithmetic, encoding-seam specifics and exact budgets are summarized rather than serialized. A reader can reconstruct the SHAPE and the backtracking behaviour of the emitted matcher; a reader cannot regenerate the matcher.
- <a id="s1-p2"></a>[1¶2] It is not an IR in the compiler sense. `--emit-ir` is a byproduct of the emitter's walk, not an input anything consumes.
- <a id="s1-p3"></a>[1¶3] It is VM-only. `--emit-ir` on a pure-DFA artifact REFUSES, naming `--engine=vm` as the way to get a VM program. There is no DFA or prefilter listing section and no `--emit-dot`.
- <a id="s1-p4"></a>[1¶4] It derives from the emitter's own walk, and this is the format's one absolute constraint (`docs/design/engine_m4.md` §10): every row is rendered from the `VEvent` stream the emitting call itself appended. The listing is never a second description of what the emitter does. A renderer consumes that event stream and does not re-walk the AST or the DFA.
- <a id="s1-p5"></a>[1¶5] It is a query like `--emit-facts` (`facts_listing.md` §2): it takes a pattern and no `-o`, and `--emit-ir --emit-facts` is refused as two separate queries.

<a id="s2"></a>
## 2. Framing

1. <a id="s2-p1"></a>[2¶1] `docs/spec/table_contract.md` applies in full: TAB-separated values, `#` comment lines, the last `#` line before a section's first data row is that section's header, columns are append-only, an empty field means "none", a field never contains a TAB.
2. <a id="s2-p2"></a>[2¶2] Every table is a NAMED `#section`, the PROGRAM body included. There is no anonymous section and no sibling line-oriented format. Nine sections are printed, in this order: `summary`, `slots`, `rungs`, `strategies`, `pruning`, `program`, `choicepoints`, `islands`, `callouts`.
3. <a id="s2-p3"></a>[2¶3] Column WIDTH is not a contract. Fields are unpadded.
4. <a id="s2-p4"></a>[2¶4] The section NAME set is the API and is append-only. A name, once shipped, keeps its meaning; new sections may be added. The same rule holds for each section's columns, independently.
5. <a id="s2-p5"></a>[2¶5] Cell escaping is `pcrec_sb_text`'s vocabulary, the one every registry TSV dump uses: a byte below 0x20, and 0x7f, goes out as `\xNN`; every other byte (backslash and high bytes included) passes through as itself. It protects the FRAME and never transcodes content. It is NOT `pcrec_sb_field`'s round-trippable `.rxt` escape, and the two are not interchangeable.
6. <a id="s2-p6"></a>[2¶6] A multi-valued cell is comma-joined with no spaces (`cursor,revdet`). `summary`'s `rungs` and `strategies` values use it. `summary`'s `possessify` value is the one SLASH-joined pair (`marked/total`).
7. <a id="s2-p7"></a>[2¶7] A `#` line never follows a section's data. An empty population is therefore a ROW whose cells are empty and whose `note` carries the sentence, never a comment.
8. <a id="s2-p8"></a>[2¶8] The preamble before the first `#section` is free prose and belongs to no section.

<a id="s3"></a>
## 3. The sections

<a id="s3-1"></a>
### 3.1 `summary` — `fact | value | note`

<a id="s3-1-p1"></a>[3.1¶1] One row per artifact-wide fact. `value` is the machine-readable half; `note` is prose for a human and carries no promise of wording (D26): what a fact IS is exact, how it is worded is not.

| `fact` | `value` |
|---|---|
| `pattern` | the pattern text, framed per §2¶5 |
| `engine` | always `vm` (this listing exists only for VM artifacts) |
| `prefilter` | one of the tokens of §3.1.1 |
| `root-minw` | the root minimum width; the row is present ONLY when it reached the analysis ceiling |
| `rungs` | comma-joined rung kinds anywhere in the program (`cursor`, `frames-bounded`, `frames-unbounded`, `revdet`, `counter`), or `none` |
| `strategies` | comma-joined strategy kinds (`possessive`, `backtracking`), or `none` |
| `possessify` | `marked/total` source quantifiers, or EMPTY when `-fno-possessify` denied the pass |
| `caps` | the capture-slot pair count (`<PREFIX>_NCAPS`) |
| `step-budget` | the backtrack-resumption budget, or EMPTY under `--fno-step-budget` |
| `resume-frames` | the stamped resume-frame capacity |
| `trail-entries` | the stamped trail capacity |
| `subject-ceiling` | the declared subject ceiling in bytes, or EMPTY when the capacities are exact |
| `labels` | emitted label count |
| `events` | listing-event count |
| `resume-points` | the PRE-PASS count the resume-point cap is checked against: an ESTIMATE, and an over-count is the safe direction |
| `max-replicas` | body replications, against `PCREC_MAX_VM_REPEAT_COPIES` |
| `prune-ceiling` | `none` / `prefilter-window` / `subject-end` (§3.1.2) |
| `prune-bound-sites` | emitted MRL bound sites |
| `prune-retreats` | runtime-term length retreats |
| `islands` | DFA-island count |
| `callout-sites` | callout-site count |

<a id="s3-1-1"></a>
#### 3.1.1 The `prefilter` value vocabulary

<a id="s3-1-1-p1"></a>[3.1.1¶1] The vocabulary is append-only, and the ORDER the emitter tests the routes in is load-bearing: the construct and analysis routes are decided before the flag routes, so the listing never names a flag the caller did not pass. The tokens:

| token | means |
|---|---|
| `yes` | exact capture-erased forward+reverse DFA pair |
| `yes-collapsed` | built from the count-collapsed superset |
| `no-backreference` | a backreference; no flag changes it |
| `no-linked-call` | a LINKED subroutine call; `-fprefilter` refuses |
| `no-variable` | a `${...}` variable; no flag changes it and `-fprefilter` refuses |
| `no-nullable-exact` | the pattern's own exact language admits an empty match not confined by a non-multiline start AND end anchor (the `empty_admits` fact, `facts_listing.md` §4.1.2) |
| `no-nullable-collapsed` | a size or state-cap rung offered the collapsed filter and it was declined because the collapsed language admits an empty match |
| `no-dfa-overflow` | the auto-selected prefilter's DFA build hit a cap; the `note` carries the cap text |
| `no-size-cap` | the size-cap ladder's last rung dropped the prefilter (`limits.md` §8) |
| `no-fno-prefilter` | forced off by `-fno-prefilter` |
| `no-engine-vm` | the `--engine=vm` side effect |

<a id="s3-1-2"></a>
#### 3.1.2 `prune-ceiling`

<a id="s3-1-2-p1"></a>[3.1.2¶1] `prune-ceiling` uses the same three words as the artifact's own `<PREFIX>_VM_PRUNE_CEILING` stamp. The two are computed INDEPENDENTLY, so a consumer can compare them by equality. This row's `none` means `-fno-length-prune`; the stamp's `none` means no bound site was emitted. The two agree on every artifact that clamps, which is the population any check about them is scoped to.

<a id="s3-2"></a>
### 3.2 `slots` — `family | slot | holds | note`

- <a id="s3-2-p1"></a>[3.2¶1] The `slot_values` layout (`docs/design/engine_m4.md` §2.4), derived from the same accessors the emitter indexes with. "Written" is derived from the `VE_SET` events, so a slot the layout reserves and the program never writes shows up as exactly that.
- <a id="s3-2-p2"></a>[3.2¶2] `family` is a fixed vocabulary, append-only: `group`, `guard`, `low`, `mark`, `revdet`, `lookmark`, `lookpos`.
- <a id="s3-2-p3"></a>[3.2¶3] Every family contributes at least one row. A family with no slots emits one row with `slot` and `holds` empty, carrying its explanation (where it has one) in `note`. "Which families does this artifact use" is therefore a projection of a declared column.
- <a id="s3-2-p4"></a>[3.2¶4] `group` is the one family whose `slot` cell names a PAIR (`2,3`): a capture group owns its start and its end together and the written verdict is a property of the pair. Every other family's `slot` is a single number.
- <a id="s3-2-p5"></a>[3.2¶5] `revdet` is the one family with THREE rows per loop index, in the order entry, low-water, ceiling.

<a id="s3-3"></a>
### 3.3 `rungs`, `strategies`, `pruning` — `label | kind | detail`

- <a id="s3-3-p1"></a>[3.3¶1] These are the PER-QUANTIFIER views of the `VE_RUNG` / `VE_STRAT` / `VE_PRUNE` event streams: one row per emitted quantifier, in emission order, `label` naming the label the decision was recorded against and `kind` the decision.
- <a id="s3-3-p2"></a>[3.3¶2] Each row is appended by the same call that decided the emitted shape, so a row and the code it describes are one fact recorded once.
- <a id="s3-3-p3"></a>[3.3¶3] An empty population is one row with `label` and `kind` empty and the reason in `detail`.
- <a id="s3-3-p4"></a>[3.3¶4] These are per EMITTED quantifier. `summary`'s `possessify` is per SOURCE quantifier, and the two populations differ whenever a bounded repeat replicates its body.

<a id="s3-4"></a>
### 3.4 `program` — `label | op | args | target | note`

<a id="s3-4-p1"></a>[3.4¶1] The straight-line trace of what executes. `op` is the instruction word and is the column a consumer selects on; `args` is its operand; `target` is the label control reaches; `note` is the role text the walk recorded.

| `op` | `label` | `args` | `target` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | the label (`L7`, or `accept` / `fail` for the two terminals) | — | — |
| `consume` | — | the class/character description | the next label |
| `compare` | — | a literal run, `'<bytes>' (N bytes)`: printable ASCII as itself, anything else (and `\` and `'`) as `\xNN` (`tuning.md` §2.31) | the next label |
| `assert` | — | the assertion's description | the next label |
| `push` | — | — | the RESUME label |
| `set` | — | `slot_values[N] <- scan_position` | — |
| `goto` | — | — | the target label |
| `fail` | — | — | — |
| `note` | — | — | — |
| `accept` | — | — | — |
| `call` | — | the CALLEE label | the RETURN label |
| `return` | — | `goto* frame.call_ret` | — |
| `cut` | — | `frames <- slot_values[N]` | — |

<a id="s3-4-p2"></a>[3.4¶2] `op` is append-only as a vocabulary. Rung, strategy and prune events write no C of their own and therefore appear in their own sections only, never here.

<a id="s3-5"></a>
### 3.5 `choicepoints` — `label | resume | note`

<a id="s3-5-p1"></a>[3.5¶1] One row per emitted resume-frame push: `label` is the site, `resume` is the label the frame resumes. Preference order: the frame pushed at a site resumes the LESS preferred alternative. A program that never backtracks emits one empty row saying so.

<a id="s3-6"></a>
### 3.6 `islands` — `label | width | note`

<a id="s3-6-p1"></a>[3.6¶1] One row per emitted DFA island (`docs/spec/tuning.md` §2.20). The COUNT is `summary`'s `islands` row. An empty population is one empty row with the reason.

<a id="s3-7"></a>
### 3.7 `callouts` — `label | note`

<a id="s3-7-p1"></a>[3.7¶1] One row per emitted callout site. The COUNT is `summary`'s `callout-sites` row. Module `callouts` has no producer, so this section is empty on every artifact.

<a id="s4"></a>
## 4. Consuming it

- <a id="s4-p1"></a>[4¶1] `tests/lib/table.sh` is the in-tree implementation of both contracts: `table_section_rows FILE SECTION`, `table_field FILE SECTION COL`, `table_lookup FILE SECTION KEYCOL KEY VALCOL`, `table_col_index`, `table_check_truthfulness`. Each fails loudly on an absent section, column or key.
- <a id="s4-p2"></a>[4¶2] A consumer resolves sections and columns by name. A fixed-position `grep` against this listing is not supported: the format's declaration-based parsing exists so that a consumer does not depend on position.
